sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Card imports
sections.what: Brings in React, the animation library and the class-combining helper.
sections.why: Likely reason: the animation library provides the hover lift and the helper merges the card's styles.
sections.watch_out: The card depends on the animation library, so removing that package breaks every card.

sections.name: CardProps
sections.title: Card options and panel look
sections.what: Defines the card's options: a glow color (indigo, emerald, amber, rose or none) and a gradient flag. Draws a rounded panel with a border that lifts slightly on hover.
sections.why: Likely reason: one panel look is reused across the app, and the glow marks important cards.
sections.watch_out: The gradient option has no visible effect, and the rose glow matches the indigo glow, so callers may expect differences that are not there.

summary: A rounded panel with a thin border that lifts slightly on hover, used as the container for content.
purpose: Give content panels one consistent look across the app.
why: Likely reason: panels share one style, and a glow option marks cards that need attention.
how: 1. Takes the content and optional glow and gradient settings. 2. Picks the glow border color, or none. 3. Draws a panel with the base style, the glow style and any extra styles. 4. Adds a small upward movement on hover with a spring effect.
inputs: Content inside the card, an optional glow color, an optional gradient flag, and extra class names or animation settings.
outputs: A styled panel on screen. Nothing is saved.
risks: The gradient option is accepted but adds no visible change. The rose glow uses the same color as indigo.
debug: If a card does not show its glow, check the glow name passed in. If a card does not lift on hover, check the animation library setup.
